stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-8eba741f: bottom-anchored column continuation

## Verified rule
In the demonstrated 17x17 instances, the bottom row contains repeated colored markers (example: colors 5 at columns 5, 9, 14 in the demo; test bottom row had color 5 at columns 5, 8, 11). These identify the columns to extend upward. For each marked column, propagate upward the nearest nonzero color encountered below: equivalently scan each selected column from bottom to top, carrying its most recent nonzero value, and replace zero cells with that carried value. Preserve all original nonzero cells and every other column unchanged. The bottom-row markers themselves are part of the source color runs. The test with markers in cols 5/8/11 was answered correctly by filling these full columns with successive source values, preserving source color transitions (e.g. col 5: 5 below row 7, 8 above row 7; col 8: 5 at bottom, 6 at rows 12-14, 1 rows 4-11, 8 at top; col 11: 5 bottom, 4 rows 10-14, 7 rows 7-9, 3 rows 0-6).

## Demo evidence / direction
Demo 1 showed bottom-row markers at columns 5, 9, 14. Outputs constructed vertical color bands in exactly these columns, preserving the nonzero seeds and extending nearest-seed colors upward: column 5 filled with 2 from rows 3-13, then 5 below and original 8/9/1 above; column 9 filled with 4 over its gaps down through row 14, retaining the original 7 and 4 seeds; column 14 filled with 6 below the 9 seed at row 4 and 9 above it. Other cells remained unchanged. Thus do not globally fill rows/other columns; bottom-row markers select the columns, and source values segment each fill.

## Procedure
1. Find nonzero columns in the bottom row; treat each as a selected column.
2. Scan each selected column from bottom to top, retaining the most recent nonzero value; replace zeros with that value. Preserve original nonzeros.
3. Leave all unselected columns untouched.
4. Validate all output differences occur only in selected columns and each filled run carries the nearest lower seed color."
}
